When non-induction looks like dormancy: a first-passage feedback model and its empirical limits

In a finite observation window, "not yet growing" and "unable to grow" leave the same record. A three-term feedback circuit makes the first-passage survival exactly computable and exactly checkable against simulation, a screened public dataset shows what the record can add, and a short proposition states where every finite window stops.

Zheng Haobo · Control and Computation in Biological Systems (EST 5053), Westlake University · Research essay (Assignment 4) · November 2026

Shift a culture of genetically identical bacteria from a comfortable carbon source to a poor one, and the cells do not agree on what to do next. After a glucose-to-acetate shift, about half of an Escherichia coli population enters sustained growth; after a shift to fumarate, the paper reports that "only 0.1% of the cells resumed growth", about one cell in a thousand.1 In a different experiment, the paper reports, cells shifted from glucose to lactose all pass through a growth arrest of stochastic length, and the times at which they switch on their lactose-utilizing machinery spread bimodally: about 30 percent within 50 minutes, the rest between one and three hours.2 Arrested is not dead. In the fumarate experiment, plate counts equaled total cell counts at every time point, and the non-growing cells resumed growth when glucose returned. In a Lactococcus lactis version of the same switch, the non-switching cells divide again once glucose is added.13

Every such observation hides a clock, and the clock is only partly observable. Give each cell a private starting time L, the time at which the tracked event would happen if the cell were followed forever. An experiment with window T that also loses cells along the way records, for each lineage, the earlier of the event and the last observation: Y=min⁡(L,C) with an indicator of which happened, where C=min⁡(T,U) and U is the time the lineage leaves observation. A lineage seen to start gives L itself. A lineage that goes quiet gives only a lower bound, L>C. Cells that would start at hour seven and cells that would never start are the same record at hour six, and the fraction still quiet at T is the value SL(T)=P(L>T) of the survival function, a function of the window before it is a fact about cells. One warning comes with the notation. L names a different random variable in every experiment: time to resumed growth in the arrest experiments, time to induction of a reporter in the fluorescence experiments. They are different quantities with different distributions, and this essay keeps the name attached to the readout. The limit of what this record can decide is itself a theorem, proved as a short proposition in section 6: a finite window constrains the survival function on [0,T] and leaves the tail beyond it not uniquely determined.

This essay builds the smallest circuit that makes the waiting problem concrete: a trickle of bursty leak expression, cooperative positive-feedback production, and first-order loss. Below the threshold set by these terms the circuit is a finite absorbing Markov chain, so the fraction of cells that have not crossed by time T is one matrix exponential, and it can be checked against exact stochastic simulation with no fitted parameters. The essay carries that computation through, checks it exactly, and then asks what a public single-cell dataset, screened to the original paper's own sample, can add. The answer has two halves. The computation validates to the binomial resolution of the simulation, and the screened data give a clean descriptive anchor: a survival curve, a strong trench-level association, and a low tail of cells that were already near growth arrest at the switch. But the mechanisms behind those records, a permanent nonresponding class, a shared microenvironment, and an inherited cellular state, are exactly the things a finite window cannot separate. Nothing here is offered as a new method or a new mechanism.

How to read this

The argument runs along a five-link chain, and the letters name the links: P for the problem, the question and why it matters; C for the challenge, why it is not already answered; A for the approach, what this essay does about it; P for the proof, the derivation, the numbers, and the simulation; and S for the significance, what changes if the argument is right. Section 1 states the problem (P); section 2 reads the six papers that fix what is already known; section 3 states the challenge the record poses (C). Sections 4 and 5 build the circuit and define the first-passage waiting problem (A). Section 6 computes the survival exactly, validates it against exact simulation, and proves the finite-window proposition; sections 7 and 8 screen and analyse the public single-cell dataset with right censoring and clustering made explicit (P). Section 9 documents how every number was produced and how to recompute it, and section 10 restates the argument the computation supports and what would change if it holds (S). Concepts such as first passage, censoring, the Kaplan–Meier estimate, and the intraclass correlation are each taught in a sentence or two where they first appear. Every quantitative claim carries a superscript to a reference or a pointer to the provenance notes in section 9.

Part I

The problem in the window

What the fate split looks like, what the six defining papers established, and what a usable answer has to do.

1Problem: A population that splits, and the window that hides why

The fate split is easy to see. The question is what it is a split of, and the observation window decides what the record can show.

The experiments behind this essay's question come in two formats. In the split format, a population divides into growers and non-growers. Kotte and colleagues shifted E. coli from glucose to gluconeogenic carbon sources and followed membrane-dye dilution in stained populations by flow cytometry. On acetate, the growing subpopulation settled near half the population; on fumarate, near one in a thousand.1 The non-growing cells stayed viable: for the fumarate shift, plate counts equaled total counts at every time point, and non-growing cells resumed growth when returned to glucose.1 In the waiting format, arrest is close to universal but temporary, and what differs between cells is timing. Julou and colleagues tracked E. coli through a glucose-to-lactose shift in a mother machine: the paper reports that every cell enters a growth arrest right after the switch, and the moment at which its lactose machinery, a LacZ-GFP fusion, becomes detectable arrives within 50 minutes for about 30 percent of cells and between one and three hours for the rest.2

Both formats invite the same word, dormancy, and the word is where the trouble starts. This essay uses it only as a three-clause label:

Definition (dormancy, used throughout)

A cell is dormant with respect to an observation window of length T when three things hold: (i) it does not grow during the window; (ii) it is alive at the end of it; (iii) it resumes growth when conditions improve. The clauses are independent claims. Failure to grow is the only clause a microscope sees directly. Viability and resuscitation each need a measurement of their own, and in the studies used here they were established for bulk or enriched populations, not for each tracked cell.

Neither format, as recorded, decides between the interpretations. In the split format, the non-growing fraction could be a stable type or the visible part of a very wide waiting distribution. In the waiting format, the original paper's population-level statement that "almost all cells eventually induce their lac operon" is a claim over finite windows and specific conditions. It is compatible with every cell having a finite starting time, and equally compatible with a small subpopulation that would never start.2 What the record gives at window T is a nonresponse fraction: an estimate of the value SL(T)=P(L>T) that the survival function of the readout's starting time takes at the window length, with the censoring bookkeeping of the opening section attached. Different mechanisms are different distributions of L, so the object to compute is not a yes-or-no type but a waiting-time distribution. That value is sometimes loosely called the "dormant fraction". The label is not adopted here: nonresponse alone establishes none of the three dormancy clauses; even direct absence of growth would establish only the first, and a censored induction record shows neither.

Non-induction is not dormancy

In the fluorescence experiments the record shows induction, not growth, and the two come apart at both ends. About 3 percent of the cells in the Julou experiment induced their lac operon but did not restart growing, so induction does not guarantee growth.2 Conversely, a cell that has not induced by T is a censored observation, not a phenotype: nothing in that record shows it alive or able to resume. Viability of non-growers is established for the split experiments on other substrates and in other organisms, not for the uninduced cells of the lac experiment.13 This essay therefore computes non-induction fractions and marks every dormancy inference as a separate, weaker claim.

The limit of what this record can decide deserves a precise statement, because the essay's model will live inside it. Section 6 proves a short proposition to that effect: a finite window constrains the survival function on [0,T] and no more. The tail would stay undetermined even if that restriction were known without error: every tail mass up to the bound the record already places on the never-responding mass induces the same finite-window observations. Everything the essay computes, and everything the data show, lives on the inside of that boundary.

2Six papers, one measurement problem

The pieces this essay uses were built by six studies. Reading them as one conversation fixes what is known and what this computation is for.

The split and its mechanism. Kotte and colleagues showed that the grow-or-arrest split of the glucose shift is generated at the shift itself: flux through the carbon backbone feeds back on the Cra regulator, producing two self-consistent metabolic states separated by a watershed, and a cell's state at the shift decides which side it lands on.1 Their model is deterministic: it contains no stochastic escape between the states and no explicit waiting distribution, and their experiments detected no switching between phenotypes on the gluconeogenic source.

Further, flow cytometry uncovered no evidence of stochastic inter-phenotype switching on the gluconeogenic carbon source, indicating that the two phenotypes were stable. Kotte et al., 2014

The waiting time and its trigger. For the lac operon the single-cell record is different. With the artificial inducer TMG, Choi and colleagues watched single cells and found that induction is triggered by rare large bursts: complete dissociation of the repressor from the DNA "result[s] in large bursts of permease expression that trigger induction", with a threshold near 375 permeases under those conditions.4 Julou and colleagues then made the switch with the natural inducer and found the opposite regime: basal lac expression is so low that many cells hold zero LacZ at the switch, the trigger threshold is "on the order of a single molecule", those sensorless cells simply wait for a stochastic burst, and the circuit needs no bistability at all.2 The two thresholds are not in conflict: they were measured under different inducers, for different proteins, in different experimental designs. Both studies characterized the waiting distribution itself: its bimodality, its control by pre-existing expression, its consequences for population growth. Neither set out to produce the object this essay starts from, the non-induction fraction as an explicit function of the window, computed from a mechanism and compared with censored single-cell records. Whether that object is worth computing is exactly what the rest of the essay tests.

Memory and the physical clock. Lambert and Kussell measured how long lac induction persists through glucose growth and found the answer in dilution: LacZ and LacY degrade so slowly that "the main factor that decreases internal levels of lac proteins is dilution due to cell growth". Memory protects a cell from a lag for about four divisions and fades over ten to twelve generations.5 The Julou dilution experiments agree, with LacZ-GFP halving at each division and the lag distribution relaxing back to the naive pattern over roughly sixteen divisions.2 This fixes the physical timescale of protein loss in growing cells, the benchmark any molecular reading of a fitted loss term has to respect.

Viability across systems, and the shape of long waits. Two further studies bound the interpretations. Solopova and colleagues watched the glucose-to-cellobiose shift of L. lactis at single-cell resolution and observed "two stable phenotypes: cells that have switched and use cellobiose and cells that never make the switch". The non-switching cells "are not dead", and divide readily once glucose is added. The split is shaped by the stringent response and tuned by preculture, a bet-hedging reading of the same window problem.3 Himeoka and Kaneko found in a coarse-grained model of starvation and refeeding that cell-to-cell lag distributions develop a broad shape with an exponential long-time tail, and reported good agreement with data at 24 and 48 hours of starvation while noting that longer starvations may carry an even longer tail. A long tail in a different coarse-grained model is a caution for this essay, not a confirmation: it shows that a long tail alone does not uniquely identify any one mechanism, including ours (cited from the arXiv v1 preprint).6

Read as one conversation, the record is: a threshold-and-initial-state mechanism for the split, a single-molecule trigger and a waiting picture for the lac system, a dilution clock for protein memory, viability of non-growers in adjacent systems, and modeled waits whose long-time tail is exponential in at least one coarse-grained model, so a long tail alone identifies no mechanism. What follows does not open a hole in that record. It builds a deliberately small model that contains the shared structure, computes one window quantity exactly, holds the computation against exact simulation, states the proposition that bounds what any window can decide, and then reads a screened public dataset with the emphasis on where the record stops.

3Challenge: What a usable answer needs

Three obstacles stand between the phenomenon and a computed answer, and each one shapes the design of the model and the reading of the data.

Obstacle one: feedback plus cooperativity makes the present a poor witness to the future. Positive feedback means production increases with its own product. With a sufficiently S-shaped production response, which the circuit of section 4 assumes explicitly, the deterministic limit of such a circuit has two stable states separated by an unstable one. A cell's current state then does not determine its fate: a cell below the threshold today may still cross tomorrow, and a cell above it can fall back. Any finite window confuses two populations that a steady-state view merges: cells that will never cross and cells that have not crossed yet. The two corresponding model quantities, the never-crossed fraction and the below-threshold fraction at T, are different objects, and both can be computed from the same Markov chain: the never-crossed fraction needs only the states below the threshold, while the below-threshold fraction needs the whole, truncated state space. The first is not special because it alone is computable. It is convenient because its computation stays finite and exact. A model that wants to say anything about windows must track the crossing event itself, not the current state.

Obstacle two: readouts are not interchangeable. Growth arrest, induction of a reporter, colony formation, and resuscitation after refeeding measure different events on different clocks, and the private starting time L changes name and meaning with each. The fluorescence readout is the one this essay confronts with data, and it is treacherous in a specific way: the recorded lag in the Julou experiment is the time at which LacZ-GFP has accumulated by roughly 200 molecules, which is the sum of a waiting part, up to the trigger, and a production part, after it.2 The lag is therefore not the first-passage time of the trigger even when the trigger is a single molecule, and a mechanism can be mapped onto such data only through an observation model that says which of the two clocks the record reads.

Obstacle three: the cells are not independent samples. In a mother machine, the cells of one growth channel share that channel's environment and commonly descend from a small set of related founders, though not always a single one. If the relevant cell state is shared at that level, treating the tracked lineages as independent observations counts the same information many times. This is not a technicality. In the dataset of sections 7 and 8, lineages of one growth channel are strongly associated in their induction lags: the intraclass correlation among slow induced records reaches 0.77 on the paper's own quality-controlled sample, while a within-day permutation null never exceeds 0.03 (section 8). One caution belongs with the number itself. The intraclass correlation, the fraction of a trait's variance that lies between groups rather than within them, is a statement about records: it establishes that the data organize by channel, not which biological quantity is shared. Section 8 keeps the two apart.

The requirement these three obstacles impose

A usable answer has to (i) compute the crossing event, not the current state; (ii) state the readout precisely, because the recorded time in a fluorescence experiment contains production after the trigger and is not the bare waiting time; and (iii) quantify the shared structure in the data and carry it as a limitation instead of pretending the cells are independent. The circuit of Part II is built for (i) and (ii), and the re-analysis of Part III treats (iii) as a boundary on its claims.

Part II

A circuit small enough to compute

Three terms, one threshold, a first-passage problem solved exactly and checked exactly, and the proposition that bounds what any window can decide.

4Approach: Three terms: bursty leak, cooperative production, loss

A three-term circuit with a threshold: what each term means, why the production term must be cooperative for a threshold to exist at all, and what every symbol is allowed to mean.

To use carbon source B (after growth on carbon source A), a cell needs a class of key proteins: transporters that import B, and enzymes that process it. Let n be the molecule count of this class and Ω the copy-number scale, so that e=n/Ω is a dimensionless relative amount. Each molecule is removed at a constant loss rate, taken as one, and this rate is what defines the time unit: one model time unit is one mean molecule lifetime against loss, and all model windows T in this part are dimensionless multiples of it. The loss rate carries no calibration to laboratory minutes, and this essay never equates a model window with an experimental one. n is always an integer, and every cell runs the same three-term rule. There are no pre-labeled grower and dormant types.

Bursty leak. With the operon uninduced, basal expression still fires in translational bursts: bursts arrive at rate Ωβ/b and add a geometrically distributed number of molecules with mean b, defined for b≥1 on the counts 1, 2, 3…, with b=1 the single-molecule burst, for a mean leak of Ωβ molecules per time unit. Cooperative production. The key proteins bring in carbon and energy, and production of more key protein increases with the amount already present: production per time unit is ΩV⁡h(e) with h(e)= e21+e2 , the saturation constant set to one, which defines the unit of e. Loss. The removal at unit rate stands for degradation, inactivation, or dilution by growth when the cell grows. In a non-growing state dilution is not available, so there the term stands for degradation or inactivation. It is an effective first-order assumption about net loss, not a measured maintenance budget, and no claim about energy or cost is attached to it.

For large copy number, the deterministic limit of this counting process is

dedt = β + V⁡e21+e2 − e (1)

Three cautions attach to equation (1). It is the large-Ω mean-field limit, not an exact equation for the average at finite copy number: the production function is curved, so the average of h(n/Ω) is not h of the average, and that difference is precisely the fluctuation that sections 5 and 6 are about. The feedback lives in the production term: production increases with e, which is all "positive feedback" means here. The loss term −e is a separate restoring contribution, not a second feedback loop: the low state is simply where leak production balances loss. And the circuit carries no resource budget of its own, and this essay assumes no growth law: no mapping from these protein states to growth rates is fitted or used, and the experiments of Part III are read through the lag readout alone. The "high state" below is a high protein level, not a measured growth state.

Why production must be cooperative here. Consider first the monotone saturating alternative h(e)=e1+e . Setting the drift to zero and multiplying by 1+e gives

e2 −(V+β−1)e −β =0, (2)

whose roots multiply to −β<0: for β>0 and any V≥0, exactly one root is positive, so the deterministic circuit has a single stable state and no threshold, at any gain. (β=0 is the boundary case, where e=0 itself becomes a fixed point.) The cooperative form behaves differently. Setting the drift to zero and multiplying by 1+e2, the fixed points of equation (1) are the positive roots of

e3 −(V+β)e2 +e−β =0 (3)

Whether the cubic has three positive roots is a question about the gain window. The gain must be large enough that a high state exists, and small enough that the leak floor survives: near the origin production is approximately Ve2, and the floor together with the unstable root exists only while 4Vβ<1, approximately. At larger gain the drift is positive all the way up, the low state has disappeared, and every cell flows upward. Both production forms are positive feedback in the sense above. Only the cooperative shape yields the two-state structure, and the square in h is a phenomenological choice: cubic or other sigmoidal forms would serve the same role, and the empirical content of the assumption is only that production is sufficiently S-shaped.

When the three roots exist, their character follows from the slope of the drift g(e)=β+Vh(e)−e: a fixed point is stable when g′(e)=Vh′(e)−1 is negative, because the drift then points back toward it from both sides. At the low root el≈β the production slope is tiny, so the state is stable: leak balanced by loss. At the saturated high root eh≈V the slope is tiny again, so it is stable too. Between them sits a root where h′>1/V, the unstable fixed point e∗. The drift points down everywhere between the low state and the unstable root, pulling the count back toward the floor, and points up everywhere between the unstable root and the high state. The unstable root is the watershed the count has to cross, and its molecule count ns=e∗Ω is the threshold. The gain moves the threshold, and the rest of the landscape with it.

The environment reaches the circuit through several parameters at once, not only through the threshold. Raising leak β, as a small dose of the inducer IPTG does by relieving LacI repression, lifts the low state and raises the burst arrival, which shortens the wait; the original study used low doses of exactly this inducer and observed the shortened lags that relief of repression predicts.2 Raising gain V, say by richer substrate or better transporters, lowers the unstable root and raises the high state, so it shortens the multi-molecule wait and lifts the plateau. A real substrate change need not act on V alone, and the model carries no energy budget that would say which knob it moves. Either way, no knob moves only one landmark. Loss depends on the cell's growth state. None of these knobs is redundant, and part of the work of Part III is to keep them apart when reading data.

Definition (capacity, used from here on)

Cell state enters the circuit through one multiplier φ, the cell's production capacity for this class of proteins. Capacity scales both production terms alike: the burst arrival Ωβ/b and the feedback gain V are both multiplied by φ, so the leak-to-gain ratio is unchanged and only the overall production capacity moves. The baseline is φ=1. The essay assumes 0<φ≤1, the normalized range of a capacity response that can only reduce synthesis below a reference cell's; values φ>1 appear only as mathematical extensions of equation (6). Two qualifications attach. That the same φ acts before and after the switch, as every computation below assumes, is an experimental-protocol assumption of the calculation, not a verified response. And nothing here measures a cell's φ; section 6 works out what the assumption does to the fixed points.

Terms, named once

Bursty birth: leak expression in translational bursts of mean size b≥1 at mean rate Ωβ. Cooperative production: feedback synthesis ΩV⁡h(e) with S-shaped h. Loss: first-order removal at unit rate per molecule, which defines the time unit. Threshold: the unstable fixed point's molecule count ns. For β=0.02, V=3.2, the threshold is 6.5 molecules at Ω=20 and 16.2 at Ω=50.

5Approach: Integer counts make the threshold a waiting problem

With integer counts and realistic copy numbers, most cells start below the threshold, and the fate question becomes: how long does the first crossing take?

Before the switch, the cell lived in carbon source A, where B-specific proteins bring no benefit and the feedback term is inactive. The count n then fluctuates under bursty birth and loss alone. The model assumes the pre-switch period is long enough that the count has reached the stationary distribution p0 of that leak-loss process. This is an assumption about the experiment, not a property the data verify here. The stationary law has a closed form, which the essay uses: for single-molecule bursts (b=1) it is Poisson with mean Ωφβ, and for larger bursts it is negative-binomial with shape Ωφβ/(b−1) and success probability 1/b, with mean Ωφβ in both cases. Here φ is the capacity multiplier defined at the end of section 4, which scales leak and feedback alike. At the switch the feedback turns on, and every cell evolves under the full rule from wherever it happens to be. Since ns is several molecules while the starting average is a fraction of one, the typical cell starts below the threshold and must wait for bursts and feedback births to carry it across. The time of the first crossing is a first-passage time, and its distribution is the object.

Definition (the two window quantities)

With ns the threshold molecule count and M=⌈ns⌉ its integer ceiling: A(T) is the probability that the count has never reached ns by time T, the survival function of the first-passage time. D(T) is the probability of sitting below the threshold at T, whatever the history. They differ by the cells that crossed and later fell back below ns, which count in D but not in A. A cell already at or above the threshold at the switch counts as crossed at time zero, so the convention is unconditional and A(0)=P(n0<M)≤1, with D(0)=A(0). The survival of cells that start below the threshold is A(T)/A(0). A is monotone in the window; D need not be, because cells leave and re-enter the low side of the threshold.

Conflating "never crossed" with "currently below threshold" is the same window fallacy as section 1, now inside the model, and the two quantities answer different questions: A(T) is about the waiting time, D(T) about the state at one instant. The model makes the difference large, not subtle. At the validated configuration Ω=10, V=2.8, β=0.02, b=1, φ=1 (threshold 4 molecules), essentially every cell has crossed by T=400: A(400)=0.0015, yet D(400)=0.344, so 34 percent of the cells are below the threshold at that moment, whether they crossed and returned or never crossed at all. Figure 3 plots the two curves and the gap between them. Reading the state as the fate would turn massive returns into waiting. In every configuration scanned for this essay D in fact decreased monotonically, but nothing in its definition forces that, and the two quantities diverge as above whether they decrease or not.

What non-growth here does and does not mean

Everything computed in Part II concerns the non-induction side of the definition in section 1: fractions of cells below a protein threshold. A(T) is not "the dormancy fraction", and nothing in the circuit establishes viability or resuscitation. The circuit with β>0 and a finite threshold M produces no permanent non-inducers, and the argument needs no burst larger than a single molecule. With β>0 the burst arrival rate is positive at every count, so from any state below M there is a finite sequence of basal births that reaches M with positive probability over any fixed interval; a finite chain in which every state can reach the absorbing crossing set and no state is trapped away from it is absorbed almost surely, so A(T)→0 as T→∞. The limit needs the finite threshold and positive burst arrival, not the high state: the high state matters only because this model fixes the threshold at the unstable root, which exists just in the two-state regime. At β=0 the conclusion reverses: the count zero is absorbing, since no bursts arrive and h(0)=0 silences the feedback. At least the mass P(n0=0) then never crosses. The total never-responding mass can be larger when the initial law assigns mass to positive counts below M, from which a cell can fall to zero before ever crossing; under the stationary pre-switch law this essay uses, all mass sits at zero and the two coincide. A window-length plateau in a real population would therefore be compatible with sufficiently slow escape, with dynamics this circuit does not model, or with readout and censoring effects; it would refute the specific parameter values whose predicted escape would empty the window, not the whole family of slow-escape readings. Slow escape is one possible reading of the Kotte system's stable split, compatible with its finite observation; no calibration of that system to this model's rates has been made, so this is an interpretation, not a measured rate.

6Proof: One matrix exponential, checked against exact simulation

The never-crossed fraction needs no simulation: below the threshold the circuit is a finite absorbing Markov chain, one matrix exponential evaluates A(T), and exact stochastic simulation confirms it with no fitted parameter. The section closes with the proposition that bounds what any window can decide.

The absorbing chain and the matrix exponential

Restrict attention to states below the threshold. With M=⌈ns⌉, those are the integer counts n=0,1,…,M−1; reaching M or more means crossing, and the process is absorbed there. Within the low states, the three terms of section 4 act as jumps: a burst moves n→n+s at rate Ωφβb·1b(1−1b)s−1, a feedback birth moves n→n+1 at rate ΩφV⁡h(n/Ω), and each molecule is lost at rate one. Assemble these rates into the M×M generator Q: off-diagonal entries are the rates of the jump mechanisms whose destination stays below the threshold (a jump that crosses has no column), diagonal entries are minus the total exit rate of each state, and each row sum is non-positive, equal to minus the total rate at which jumps from that state cross the threshold, and zero for a state from which no single jump reaches the threshold. If p0 is the pre-switch stationary law, truncated to the low states, then

A(T) = p0 ⁡ exp⁡(QT) ⁡ 1 (4)

with 1 the all-ones vector: propagate the initial distribution through the absorbing chain for time T and sum what is still inside. Because p0 is truncated to the low states without renormalizing, equation (4) is the unconditional never-crossed probability under the crossed-at-time-zero convention of section 5. This is the standard transient of a finite absorbing chain, textbook material rather than a new method. The contribution claimed here is carrying it through for this circuit and validating the result against exact stochastic simulation, which is where errors in such computations usually hide.

A case solved by hand

Choose parameters so that the threshold is below one molecule: Ω=10, β=0.02, b=1, V=10, φ=1 gives ns≈0.73<1, so M=1: the only low state is n=0, where h(0)=0 and the sole exit is the next burst, at rate r=Ωφβ/b=0.2. The pre-switch count is then Poisson with mean 0.2, so P(n=0)= e−0.2≈0.819, and equation (4) collapses to a closed form: a count that starts at zero survives uncrossed to time T with probability e−rT, and averaging the exponential over the prior gives

A(T) = e−0.2(T+1) ≈ 0.819×e−0.2T , A(10)≈0.111. (5)

The first form is exact: the closed form matches the matrix exponential to 4.3×10−19 when both are evaluated unrounded, and the three-digit values 0.819 and 0.111 in the display are rounded only for reading. Exact simulation reproduces the value at T=10, which is the kind of agreement a hand-solvable case should produce. The conditioning lesson of section 5 is visible here. For a cell that starts at n=0 the mean wait is 1/r=5 time units, and mean times rate equals one, identically. Averaged over the stationary prior under the crossed-at-time-zero convention, the mean is A(0)/r≈4.1 instead: the 18 percent difference is exactly the mass 1−A(0) that already sits at or above the threshold at the switch. Any simulation check of "mean wait times rate equals one" must say which conditioning it uses, and this essay's checks use the conditional one.

Checking against exact simulation

The systematic check compares equation (4) with exact stochastic simulation: the Gillespie direct method, implemented from scratch, in which every jump is drawn from its exact waiting-time distribution and a crossing is tested at exact event times, so there is no time-step discretization to bias the comparison. Eight parameter points (P1–P8 of Table 3) were run, chosen to span the regimes the essay uses: the hand case, multi-molecule thresholds from 2 to 15 molecules, the higher-leak zone, four-molecule bursts, a halved capacity, and a point deep in the multi-molecule regime at Ω=100. Each point ran 50,000 trajectories. At each of the windows T=10,30,100,300 (and, for two points, 400), the simulated never-crossed fraction was compared with the matrix-exponential value: 34 comparisons in all, with no fitted parameter anywhere. Uncertainty is quantified by the exact two-sided binomial test of the simulated count against the master-equation probability, never by a Gaussian standard score, because six of the comparisons sit at probabilities whose expected count is far below the regime where a Gaussian approximation is meaningful. The largest absolute deviation between simulation and master equation is 5.3×10−3, at P5 and T=30 (simulated 0.2946 against exact 0.2894, exact two-sided p=0.0096, 95% interval [0.291, 0.299]). The sparse tail is judged by the same exact yardstick: at P5 and T=300, 2 of 50,000 trajectories were never crossed against an exact value of 5.9×10−6, exact p=0.036 with exact 95% interval [4.8×10−6,1.4×10−4]. The 34 comparisons share trajectories across windows, so they are correlated views of eight curves rather than 34 independent tests, and no discrepancy is claimed: the smallest exact p across the family is 0.0096, and a Bonferroni adjustment over the 34 dependent comparisons leaves the smallest family-wide value at 0.33. Figure 4 shows four representative curves (P1, P2, P4, P6) with their exact 95% intervals; the complete 34-comparison table is regenerated by the code bundle's figure stage and archived with the project (section 9). The simulation sampler itself passed self-tests on 107 draws (mean, variance, and mass of the geometric burst law and of the negative-binomial prior, all within 2.6 standard errors of truth).

What the code produced

Model-internal validation, all with no fitted parameter: fixed points by root-finding on the cubic (3); the closed-form pre-switch stationary against the truncated balance solution (agreement to 3.4×10−16 per mass point); the M=1 closed form against the matrix exponential (agreement to 4.3×10−19, both unrounded); equation (4) against 50,000-trajectory exact simulation at eight points and 34 window comparisons (largest absolute deviation 5.3×10−3 at P5, T=30; smallest exact binomial p=0.0096, family-adjusted 0.33 over the 34 dependent comparisons). Scripts V_me.py, V_ssa.py, V_me_D.py, run on the project workstation with fixed seeds recorded in the archived JSON outputs (section 9).

What the parameters do

At long times the never-crossed probability decays exponentially, A(T)≈ce−kT, where k is minus the largest real part of the eigenvalues of Q. This k is the decay rate of the tail. It is not the mean waiting time, and its inverse is a tail time constant, not an average wait. What the exact results show dramatically is how steeply the whole curve responds to the circuit parameters. At Ω=50 and V=4, raising the leak from 0.02 to 0.05 drops the never-crossed probability at T=100 from 0.840 to below 0.001 (rows 3 and 4 of Table 3, both exact and simulated). This exponential sensitivity to how far the threshold sits above the starting floor is the barrier-crossing behavior familiar from physics, and it is the mathematical reason small differences between cells can matter a great deal once several molecules must accumulate.

Cell state enters through capacity. The capacity φ of section 4 scales both production terms, because leak expression and feedback production draw on the same machinery:

dedt = φβ + φV⁡e21+e2 − e (6)

This is bookkeeping plus an assumed response, and the assumption is the whole of the mechanism: nothing here measures a cell's φ. In the small-e regime the two lower roots scale approximately as el≈φβ and e∗≈1/(φV) when the basal term is negligible in the unstable-root balance: poorer cells start from a lower floor and need more protein to break even. Both are scaling statements, not sharp values. Below a critical capacity the unstable root and the high state merge and disappear, and with them the two-state structure. The tangency sits near φcrit≈2/V for small β: the exact value at V=10, β=0.02 is 0.1992, against the approximation 0.2. Across the tested grid the small-leak approximations for the two tangencies err by at most a few percent, so they are useful guides and not exact borders. In the M=1 limit of this model, capacity enters the first-crossing wait only through the basal-arrival rate, as the next paragraph describes; the order-one trigger reported by Julou and colleagues2 does not establish that limit or rule out testing amplification and capacity mechanisms in the actual system.

Copy number has no universal direction. What raising the copy-number scale Ω does to the never-crossed fraction depends on the regime, and the model's verified points show both directions. In the one-molecule regime the wait is exponential with rate r=Ωφβ/b, set by the burst arrival alone: as long as the chain remains in the one-low-state regime M=1, raising Ω at fixed β and φ speeds the wait and lowers non-induction, and the gain V plays no role in the wait. The validated one-molecule points illustrate this, with the caveat that they differ in V as well as in Ω: from Ω=2, V=4 to Ω=10, V=10, both at β=0.02 and φ=1, A(10) drops from 0.64 to 0.11; the gain is irrelevant to this comparison only because both points sit at M=1. In the multi-molecule regime the threshold in molecules, ns=e∗Ω, rises in proportion to Ω while the initial spread grows only like its square root, and the gap to be climbed wins. The verified pair at fixed V=4 and β=0.02 illustrates the opposite pull, and it too crosses regimes rather than tracing one: Ω=2 sits at M=1 (threshold below one molecule), while Ω=50 has entered the multi-molecule regime at M=13, and raising Ω between them raises A(100) from 0.018 to 0.840. Both comparisons are exact master-equation values confirmed by simulation (Table 3). The essay claims no universality here: different regimes give different effects, and which regime a system occupies is itself a measurable question.

The trigger threshold of the Part III experiment is on the order of one molecule (section 7), which motivates reading its wait through the one-molecule limit above. That is a motivation, not an established equivalence: a threshold of order one does not by itself establish Poisson burst arrival, constant loss, this aggregate-protein model, or a homogeneous rate across cells. Nor does the model map onto the measured lag without an observation model, since the lag includes production after the trigger. The safe statement is directional: these data speak most directly to a leak-like waiting rate, and this essay fits no mapping that would license more; it does not follow that single-cell data cannot constrain an amplification mechanism in principle.

What no window can decide

The computation above is exact, but its object has a limit built into the observation itself, and everything the essay reads off data lives inside that limit. It deserves a precise statement.

Proposition (a finite window does not identify a permanent nonresponding class)

Fix a post-switch protocol and hold it fixed: L∈[0,∞] is a lineage's response time under that protocol, L=∞ meaning it never responds under it. Refeeding or otherwise changing the conditions is a different protocol and defines a different variable, which this statement does not cover. An experiment of window length T observes, for each of n lineages, (Y,Δ) with Y=min⁡(L,C) and Δ=1[L≤C], where the censoring time satisfies C≤T almost surely and is independent of L. Write S(t)=P(L>t), and suppose a candidate survival S0 on [0,T] has S0(T)>0.

(a) For every π∈[0,S0(T)] there is a survival function that agrees with S0 on [0,T] and carries exactly mass π at L=∞. (b) For a single lineage, every member of this family induces the same law of the record (Y,Δ); under ideal independent replication of the protocol, the same holds for the joint law of n records, for every n. Hence P(L=∞) is not identifiable from window- T data of any size, even in that ideal independent case; records that share an environment, as the lineages of Part III do, are weaker evidence still. (c) If S0(T)=0, every survival function agreeing with S0 on [0,T] has P(L=∞)=0. This is a statement about the population survival function; a finite sample in which every lineage responds yields only an upper confidence bound on S0(T), not the equality.

Proof. For t>T set

Sπ(t) = π+(S0(T)−π) e−ε(t−T) , Sπ(t)=S0(t) for t≤T, (7)

with ε>0. The extension has the same initial mass as S0 (Sπ(0)=S0(0), so P(L=0) is unchanged, which matters because S0(0) need not be one when L=0 carries mass); it is non-increasing and right-continuous on [0,T] because S0 is; it joins S0(T) continuously at T and decreases to π. It is therefore a valid survival function carrying an atom of mass π at L=∞. For the law of the record, condition on the censoring time. Fix C=c≤T: given c, the record is (min⁡(L,c),1[L≤c]), whose event part is the law of L restricted to [0,c] and whose censored part has mass S(c). Both are the same for every member of the family, because they agree with S0 on [0,T]. Since C≤T almost surely and the censoring law is the same under every member, the joint law of (Y,Δ) is the same for every π. No density of L is required, and S0 may have atoms. Under ideal independent replication the record law is the n-fold product of the one-record law, so it is flat in π as well. For (c), P(L=∞)≤P(L>T)=S0(T)=0. ∎

Three readings matter. First, the positive-mass part is a statement about the population survival function: it needs S0(T)>0, and a finite window in which every observed lineage responds gives only an upper bound on S0(T), tightened by more records, never replaced by the equality of part (c). Second, the flat likelihood is exact for the unconstrained extensions just constructed: within a fixed window T, more records of the same kind estimate the restriction of S to [0,T] ever more precisely, but no amount of them moves π, and a longer window only tightens the bound π≤S0(T) without ever proving the tail. Third, the flatness does not make parametric estimates meaningless. A parametric family with a built-in tail, a mixture with a never-responding class of fitted weight, or a single exponential tail, can estimate its parameters from window data and be checked on its within-window fit; but its return for P(L=∞) holds conditionally on the tail restriction the family assumes, and that restriction is exactly what the window cannot check. The returned value is a consequence of the assumed shape, not a measurement of it.

This is not new mathematics. The argument packages the classical tail freedom of censored survival data, and it is stated here because the essay's central quantity sits exactly on that freedom. Two consequences get used later. The proposition concerns nonresponse under a fixed protocol. Calling the unobserved mass dormant additionally requires the viability and resuscitation clauses of section 1, which the argument does not touch. And in the circuit of this part with β>0 the model's permanent non-inducing mass is exactly zero, so the circuit itself never produces a never-responding class; what a real-data plateau would refute is the specific parameter predictions whose escape would empty the window, not the family of slow-escape readings (section 5).

Part III

What the data show, under right censoring

The public single-cell dataset, screened to the original paper's own sample, and read with right censoring and clustering made explicit.

7Proof: The public dataset: sample screening and right censoring

The experiment puts single cells on record through a carbon switch. Which records count, and what each record type can say, decides everything that follows.

The experiment puts E. coli in the narrow channels of a mother machine, grows them in glucose, and switches the supply to lactose while tracking every cell's LacZ-GFP. For each lineage the recorded quantity is the lag: the time after the switch at which LacZ-GFP has accumulated by roughly 200 molecules. Two structural facts carry through everything below. First, the trigger threshold sits near a single LacZ molecule, established in the original study by dilution, noise, and single-molecule counting,2 which motivates reading the wait through the one-molecule limit of section 6; that reading is a working assumption, with the limits stated there, not an equivalence established by the threshold's order of magnitude. Second, as section 3 stressed, the lag is the wait plus the production needed to reach the detection level, not the first-passage time of the trigger, so the survival curve below is a curve of lags, not of bare crossing times.

Screening the sample

The published data object behind the paper's single-cell figures is a table of 8,868 recorded cell histories, of which 2,397 sit on their first lactose contact. That object is not the paper's sample. The paper's own accounting, 90 percent induced, 7 percent lost, 3 percent not induced, is computed on the seven first-switch conditions restricted to nine experiment dates: 1,633 records. The remaining records of the object sit on experiment dates that the authors themselves flagged and excluded for quality reasons, with their archived analysis notebook citing slow growth in the initial condition and lag distributions they judged anomalous (598 records from author-excluded dates), plus 166 records from a late-switch condition with a 26-hour glucose preculture that the paper's headline analysis does not use. The distinction matters exactly where this essay's question is sharpest: 45 of the 97 full-window non-inducers in the pooled object lie on author-excluded dates. This essay therefore treats the 1,633 paper-comparable records as its observational anchor and quotes pooled-object numbers only with their composition stated.

Right censoring and the record types

The observation model is the one from the essay's opening. What the record holds for each lineage is Y=min⁡(L,C) with the indicator Δ=1[L≤C], where L is the induction time and C=min⁡(T,U) the earlier of the 240-minute window and the time the lineage leaves observation. Of the 158 paper-comparable lineages without an induction event, the split matters: 52 were followed to the end of the window without inducing, which gives L>240, and 106 left earlier, which gives only L>C. The two groups carry different information, and neither is a failure. Treating all uninduced lineages as failures inflates any "never" fraction, so the analysis keeps the distinction throughout.

The survival curve. The standard tool for such records is the Kaplan–Meier estimate of the survival function. At each distinct event time tj it multiplies the estimated survival so far by the share of the risk set that does not start then:

S^L(t) = ∏j:tj≤t (1−djnj)

where nj is the risk set, the number of lineages still tracked and not yet started just before tj, and dj the number that start at tj. At tied times the events are counted first and the withdrawals leave after, so a lineage lost at minute 56 is credited with survival up to 56 and then leaves the future risk sets rather than being counted as an event. A loss is a withdrawal from follow-up, never an event. For the 1,633 paper-comparable records the estimate falls from SL(30)=0.896 through SL(60)=0.636, SL(90)=0.292, SL(120)=0.150 and SL(180)=0.056 to SL(239)=0.038 at the window's end. The risk sets at those times are 1,519, 1,046, 479, 231, 82 and 52 lineages, and the 52 still under observation at 239 minutes are exactly the full-window non-inducers, censored at the 240-minute episode end. The median event lag is 69 minutes. This curve is the empirical counterpart of the model's first-passage survival A(T), with the standing difference that its L is a lag read at a detection threshold of 200 molecules rather than at the molecular trigger threshold of the model.

Three numbers that look like one

For the 1,633 records, three quantities answer different questions and must not be mixed. The full-window non-inducer fraction is 52/1,633 = 3.2 percent. Among fate-known records only (events plus full-window non-inducers, 1,527 in all), it is 3.4 percent, but that ratio conditions on outcome ascertainment, not on follow-up completion: a record's fate is known either because an event was observed or because follow-up reached the window's end, and the ratio silently drops the 106 early-lost lineages whose outcome was never ascertained within the window. The Kaplan–Meier value SL(239)=0.038, that is, 3.8 percent, keeps the lost lineages as censored observations, and it is the only one of the three that is a survival estimate. The three numbers are close here, which is exactly why they are easy to conflate. This essay quotes each for its own question and treats none of them as a phenotype.

What the censoring is like. The censoring is early and not obviously benign. The 106 lost records were censored 15 to 198 minutes after the switch, with quartiles at 37, 56 and 75 minutes: loss of follow-up during the heart of the waiting period, not truncation at its end. The Kaplan–Meier curve is consistent for SL only under a non-informative-censoring assumption: conditional on the risk set, the lost lineages' future induction times are assumed to behave like those of the lineages still tracked. If acquisition or tracking failure correlated with growth state, the curve would be biased, and no correction is available from the published summaries. Calling the estimates descriptive does not remove that bias; it means the essay reads them as summaries of these records under the stated assumption, not as unbiased population quantities. Three measurement facts bound the early part of the curve. A recorded lag is the delay after the switch at which the LacZ-GFP level has risen by 200 molecules above a pre-induction baseline, which the original authors estimate as the mean level over the first 9 minutes after the switch (in their archived notebook, the frames between one and ten minutes after the switch, three samples at the 3-minute acquisition), a window they checked visually for induction. The notebook then searches for that crossing only among frames after the baseline window: a crossing inside the window cannot be recorded, and the earliest value the search can return is the first sample after it. This gate is a property of the estimator, not a statistical left-truncation of the sample: no record is dropped for crossing early, and a record already above the threshold at the first searchable frame is credited with that frame, still counted from the switch. Detecting an induction therefore takes at least four post-switch time points. And the smallest recorded lag in the paper-comparable sample is 21 minutes (the pooled object's minimum, 18 minutes, comes from the excluded-date records). That floor is the joint effect of the search gate, the 200-molecule threshold, and the maturation of the fluorescent protein, whose half-time is about 5.6 minutes, though a fixed maturation delay is not an exact model of the accumulation process. The curve is therefore measurement-limited below roughly the first recorded event at 21 minutes, which is one reason its fast decline starts where it does.

8Proof: Records cluster by trench, and the mechanism stays open

Cells of one growth channel start together far more than chance allows. Quantifying that association is easy. Naming the shared quantity is not, and a finite window cannot do it.

The clustering statistic

The statistic is the intraclass correlation, introduced in section 3: for records grouped by trench, the fraction of the total variance of a trait that lies between trenches rather than within them. It is zero when trench membership is irrelevant and near one when records of a trench are nearly identical. Computed on the log lag of the slow induced records (lag of 50 minutes or more), the paper-comparable sample gives 1,061 slow events in 266 trenches and an intraclass correlation of 0.767. Centering each day's values removes day-to-day variation and gives 0.752. A day-level bootstrap interval runs from 0.700 to 0.810, with the caveat that it resamples only nine experimental days, and a trench-level bootstrap interval runs from 0.709 to 0.810. The right null is a permutation: shuffle lag values between records of the same experiment day, keeping trench membership fixed, and recompute. Over 5,000 shuffles, no permuted value reached 0.03 in any of the three samples of Table 5; the Monte-Carlo permutation p is (1+0)/(5,000+1)≈2.0×10−4 in each sample, the +1-corrected Monte-Carlo value rather than an exact zero. Records of one trench differ by 15.7 minutes on average, against 33.3 minutes for records of different trenches on the same day. Per day, the correlation ranges from 0.58 to 0.85 and is positive on all nine days.

What the records do and do not share

Before reading the association, the records themselves need one check: does the same induction event enter the table twice? Three checks on the published object say no. The inclusion filter requires each recorded cell's own frames to span the switch, so a cell that divided before the switch cannot appear as a row. Within the same trench and switch, the recorded genealogy strings contain no ancestor-descendant pair of rows. And the ten birth-time coincidences that look like mother-daughter pairs all resolve to synchronously dividing aunts whose true mothers were never sampled. What the rows do share is a measurement convention: 1,559 of the 2,397 records extend past the recorded cell's own division by adding the GFP of its two daughters, so the late part of such a record is a two-cell signal, and 233 of the 1,475 paper-comparable induction events are detected on that merged post-division trace (a median of 45 minutes after the division). The merged trace is a measurement caveat for when a lag is read, not a second row for the same cell: the division and the switch are recorded as separate events, the daughters themselves have no records, and sisters give two records with disjoint frames. None of this makes the records independent, and it is not meant to: the trench is the natural cluster, and the association of Table 5 is a property of that clustering.

The low tail of the survival curve has a visible carrier. The upstream marker flags 53 records whose elongation rate before the switch fell below 4×10−5 per second, growth near arrest, and all 53 carry their own measured pre-switch slope rather than a parent's. Sixteen of them sit in the paper-comparable sample and 37 on the excluded dates, so the marker's yield concentrates where the original authors had already flagged quality problems. The arrested group is therefore a pooled subsample assembled from a quality screen, and it is read here descriptively, not as a controlled comparison group: no causal attribution is made, and no fate contrast computed across mixed samples is quoted. The original authors suspected the association: their own analysis notebook notes that cells in growth arrest before being exposed to lactose tend to have very long lags. The composition imbalance is why this essay reports the marker's reach as a sample-composition limitation rather than a quantitative fate claim.

Three mechanisms, one finite window

The same reading reconciles the two formats of section 1. The gluconeogenic-shift experiments reported their split as stable on their observation clock, which in present terms is an escape rate too small to move the split within the window: their split fraction reflects initial states against a threshold.1 Whether any of it is permanent is exactly the question the window cannot answer from inside, by the proposition of section 6.

What the association does not say

The trench-level association is a statement about records. It does not say that the cells of a trench share one biological rate, and it cannot say which quantity is shared: an inherited intracellular state, the trench's microenvironment (lactose arrival, flow, position), and the relatedness of founders are confounded by design in a mother machine. A shared launch rate is one reading of the association, adopted where needed as the minimal statistical structure that captures it, not a finding. Three mechanisms, a permanent class, a shared microenvironment, and an inherited state, can agree with the same finite-window record. The experiments that separate them are interventions, not more of the same data: reseat lineages across trenches and watch whether the association follows the lineage or the channel, move one candidate quantity and look for the response, and assay viability and resuscitation directly on the uninduced cells, without which non-induction cannot be renamed dormancy.

Part IV

Provenance and payoff

Where every number comes from, and the argument the computation supports.

9Methods and reproducibility

Where every number comes from and how to recompute it.

Model layer. All model-side numbers come from three scripts, run on the project's workstation with fixed seeds and stored verbatim as archived JSON outputs. V_me.py computes the fixed points of Table 2 by root-finding on the cubic (3), the exact tangency lines of the two-state regime, the closed-form pre-switch stationary laws and their cross-check against a truncated balance solution, and the matrix exponential of equation (4). V_ssa.py is the exact Gillespie direct-method simulator: 8 parameter points, 50,000 trajectories each, crossings tested at exact event times, seeds and configurations recorded next to every value. V_me_D.py computes the below-threshold fraction D(T) and the crossed-by-T fraction behind Figure 3 and the full-chain comparisons of section 5. The archived outputs carry the configuration, the seed, and the value side by side for every number quoted in Part II.

Data layer. The data-side numbers come from the study's published RData object (SHA-256 0720f216f07d2a7dc5528917f18c344609e2143dc4c11e3ab84e85659dff3d5f, verified before use),2 parsed with a minimal reader and reduced to a flat table, then analyzed by the project's sensitivity pipeline: sample screening (Table 4), the Kaplan–Meier curves, their risk sets, and the three estimands (section 7 and Figure 6), the intraclass correlations with day-centering and both bootstraps (Table 5), and, in section 8, the within-day permutation nulls and the growth-arrested decomposition. Outputs and a SHA-256 manifest are archived beside the essay. The lag definition, the censoring semantics, and the date-exclusion list were checked line by line against the original authors' archived analysis notebooks.

Literature layer. The six papers were read in archived full texts. The literature index records retrieval dates, file hashes, and the passages each claim rests on. Two gaps remain and are logged where they belong: the Kotte supplementary package (the main text alone supports every viability statement made here) and the Julou supplementary figure images (the captions, which are archived, support every use made here). No claim in this essay depends on either.

What is not used. Waiting-distribution fits to the pooled 2,397-record object, with a fixed production-ramp decomposition and channel-shared rates, are not used here: the pooled object mixes in the excluded dates, and no number in this essay descends from those fits.

The complete reproduction package is embedded in this page: download reproduce.zip (594 KiB, SHA-256 7cf4e99e3bab8cba30035efc897abde54ff5387c6aed356f3d2f49e97b75bcfd). Save the file, unzip it, and run python3 reproduce.py inside the package root; its README documents the verification, full, and smoke modes.

Code bundle. The downloadable bundle accompanying this essay is a portable reproduction package driven by a single entry point, reproduce.py, which locates the package root from its own file location and writes everything under outputs/. Its verification mode (python3 reproduce.py, about one minute, single core, no network) recomputes the fixed points of Table 2, the matrix-exponential values of Table 3, the closed-form cross-checks, the screening counts of Table 4, the Kaplan–Meier values and risk sets behind Figure 6 in section 7, and the intraclass correlation of Table 5 from the model definition and the packaged public input table, and checks each against the frozen archived outputs; its full mode (python3 reproduce.py --full) additionally re-runs the 8-point exact simulation, the permutation null, both cluster bootstraps, and every figure generator. The bundle contains the model scripts (me.py, ssa.py, me_d.py), the empirical pipeline (analyze_robustness.py, make_figures.py, the RData reader), the theory figure generators, the input table, and the frozen expected outputs; it needs only Python with numpy, scipy, matplotlib, and Pillow (for the figure stages), installs nothing, and downloads nothing. The statistical agreement between simulation and master equation is asserted in the bundle by the same exact binomial test reported in section 6, gated at a predeclared family-wide significance level of 0.05 with a Bonferroni adjustment over the 34 dependent comparisons, not by a Gaussian standard score.

10Significance: What the computation buys

The essay's claims, the claims it does not make, and the question it leaves behind in computable form.

What this essay does not claim

It does not claim that any cell in these experiments is permanently dormant: the computations concern finite windows, and the proposition bounds what they can decide. It does not claim mathematical novelty: the absorbing-chain transient is textbook material, and the proposition packages the classical tail freedom of censored survival data. It does not claim that the trench-level association identifies a shared biological rate, or that the low tail of growth-arrested cells is a mechanism. It does not claim viability or resuscitation for the uninduced cells of the lac experiment: that evidence lives in other systems and other substrates. It does not claim a calibrated mapping from the model's dimensionless time to experimental minutes. What it claims is narrower, and stated in full: the finite-window limit, stated exactly; the first-passage survival of a three-term feedback loop, computed exactly and validated against exact simulation with no fitted parameter; a screened, right-censored descriptive anchor in public data; and a precise statement of what would settle the open mechanisms.

The essay began with a record that hides its own question: a cell that has not responded by the end of an experiment. The three results change what can be asked about that record. First, the proposition of section 6 shows that a window of length T constrains the survival function on [0,T] and does not uniquely determine the tail beyond it. More data of the same kind estimate that restriction ever more precisely, but the never-responding mass is not an estimate waiting to converge: without an assumption about the tail it is not identified at any sample size. A longer window tightens the bound it can carry. Identifying the mass still requires a justified tail or mechanistic restriction; interventions can test such restrictions or assay viability, but a changed protocol alone does not identify permanent nonresponse under the original protocol. Second, the three-term circuit turns the fraction that has not responded into a function A(T) that is exactly computable and matches exact simulation to the binomial resolution of 50,000 trajectories with nothing adjusted, so a mechanism proposal owes a window curve, not a label. Third, the screened public data show what such a curve looks like on real cells, and they show a strong trench-level association. The data do not identify the shared biological quantity, if any, behind that association, and the same finite window leaves permanent nonresponse unidentified as well.

That is the shift this essay argues for: from a static fraction, dormant or not, to a question with a window, a readout, and assumptions, each of which can be computed, checked, and moved. The window is not a nuisance in the data. It is part of the quantity, and a mechanism that deserves the name owes us its dependence on it.
